sizing_fixed_loss:
Fixed loss sizing is trying to replace a standard linear payout of "I will risk x to make y" into an options package with equivalent loss limit. The "Risk 1 to make" slider adjusts the risk amount per target unit profit.

Given this input and a target, we use the implicit loss described in your bet to set a premium budget for the options structures we price. Note there are some structures with unlimited losses where you can lose more than the premium, please be aware of this.

To make the numbers more intuitive, all structures are sized to an amount of capital W which you can assign per trade.
sizing_kelly:
We also have the ability to size trades using the Kelly criterion. This method allows you to find optimal trade sizes for a given bet given your edge on the trade, and you can learn more about it [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_criterion). As an input for this method, we need to be able to quantify how much your view diverges from the market view across the entire distribution of potential outcomes, so you will need to provide this to the tool. If this is unclear, drop us a line and we are happy to help or clarify.

To make the numbers more intuitive, all structures are sized to an amount of capital W which is the total portfolio capital you deploy. Our implementation aims to maximise returns on this number, it is not the same as the loss tolerance for a single trade.
what:
MacroTool is a decision-support platform for translating a directional market view into specific derivative structures. It gives traders a repeatable framework for comparing different ways to express the same view, improving consistency and speed without replacing a trader’s judgement.

**The platform provides:**
- Structure comparison across 50+ candidate strategies
- Scenario- and preference-based P&L analysis to show how trades behave under different outcomes
- Kelly-based position sizing and risk-budget-based sizing
- An AI assistant for natural-language questions about trade selection, risk/reward and analytics

The tool works on mobile, but is designed for desktop.
how:
MacroTool uses a scoring framework designed to reflect how experienced traders translate a view into a trade, rather than relying solely on measures such as expected P&L, breakeven levels or back-testing.

**Recommendations are deterministic, not AI-generated.** With the same view, market data, preferences and engine configuration, the tool produces the same results every time. The framework has been built, tested and tuned by the team. It supplies every calculated number and recommendation; the LLM is only the conversational interface; it is not the pricing or risk engine.

**Current limitations:** pricing is intended for directional comparison and ranking, rather than execution-grade quotes, and will be refined. Market data is as of the date indicated, not live. Results are decision support, not a replacement for independent judgement or trade validation.
who: We are a team of traders who have spent a total of 40+ years across buy and sell side making markets in, structuring and managing risk on the whole gamut of FX options from vanilla to hybrid, DM to EM. We thought we could go a long way toward simplifying the way we approach the product set in coming up with structures to express views, so we started building this tool.
